source_message.text:
Thank you. This comparison is very helpful.

I prefer Option 1 as the baseline. I like the second V as a true proportional reduction of the Hero V.

I have one additional refinement I'd like to explore. I'd like to keep the second V the same size and see the Es and Ls reduced slightly in scale so they feel more proportional to it. The visual scale of the second V's left arm feels like a good reference.

I think this may strengthen the hierarchy between the Hero V, the alphabet, and the second V.

value_updates.cap_height_rule: Reduce the E and L slightly so their scale feels proportional to the second V, using the second V's left arm as the visual reference.

Hi Brittany,

Here is the refined proof built on our Option 1 baseline!

As requested, I reduced the scale of the E's and L's slightly so they harmonize directly with the scale and line weight of the second V's left arm.

This subtle shift strengthens the architectural rhythm across the identity, the Hero V leads, the second V maintains its distinct elevation, and the disciplined alphabet ties everything together seamlessly.

I think we have officially hit the sweet spot! I'd love to know if this delivers the exact final vision so we can lock this in, finalize the master vector assets, and wrap up ahead of Friday

source_message.text:
Hi Brittany,

Here is the refined final proof with the cap-height alignment and master geometry locked in!

Cap-Height Harmony: The top bars of the E's and L's have been scaled up slightly to match the exact height established by the top of the second V's left arm.

Signature Accent: With the left arm anchored to the cap-height, the second V's sweeping right arm now stands as the single, deliberate signature element extending subtly above the alphabet line.

Common Baseline & Baseline Kerning: Built on our winning Variation B layout, keeping the bottom points of both V's resting flush on the common baseline with tight, luxurious kerning across all letter pairs.

1:1 É Accent: Verified as a direct, unedited clone of the Hero V's right arm gesture.

I think this brings the entire architectural vision together seamlessly. If this feels complete to you, we can officially declare the logo locked and move forward with finalizing the master vector package
